div.head: VI As 8.2
div.ab: Et si eueniat, quod aliqua cognatio (tribus) ad hoc magna sit et fortis, in terra uel extra, twelfhyndes uel twihindes, ut rectum nostrum difforciet ac furem defendat, adeamus omnes una cum preposito, in cuius mannicione est (sit).

⁊ gif þonne þæt gebyrige, þæt ænig mægð to þan strang sy and to þam mycel, innon landes oððe uton landes, XIIhynde oððe twyhynde, þæt us ures rihtes wyrnen ⁊ þone þeof foren forstande, þæt we rídan be eallum mannum tó mid þam gerefan þe hit on his mónunge sy.

⁊ gif þonne þæt gebyrige, þæt ænig mægð to þan strang sy and to þam mycel, innon landes oððe uton landes, XII hynde oððe twyhynde, þæt us ures rihtes wyrnen ⁊ þone þeof foren forstande, þæt we rídan be eallum mannum tó mid þam gerefan þe hit on his mónunge sy.

Again, if it happens that any group of kinsmen — whether nobles or commoners within or beyond the borders of our district— become so strong and powerful as to prevent us from exercising our legal rights, and stand up in defence of a thief, we shall ride out against them in full force with the reeve in whose district the offence takes place.

And if it then happens that any kindred is so strong and so large, within the district or outside it, whether men of a twelve-hundred wergild or of a two-hundred, that they refuse us our rights and stand up for a thief, we are to ride thither with all our men with the reeve in whose district it is.

Und wenn nun der Fall vorkommt, dass eine Sippe so stark und so gross ist — innerhalb [dieser] Landschaft oder ausser Landes, von 1200 [Schilling Wergeld] oder 200 —, dass sie uns unser Recht verweigern und [sie] für den Dieb schützend eintritt: dass wir in gesammter Mannschaft hinzureiten mit dem [Grafschafts-]vogte, der es [Sheriff] im Bezirke jenes [Diebes] ist,

And if it then happens that a kindred is so strong and so large — within [this] district or outside it, of 1200 [shillings' wergild] or 200 — that they refuse us our right and [it] steps in to protect the thief: that we ride there with all our men, with the [shire-]reeve in whose district that [thief] is,
div.note: The Latin's ‘tþelfhyndes’, ‘tþihindes’ use þ for the OE letter wynn (w); here normalised to w. H's ‘wyrnen … forstande’ was emended by Schmid to ‘wyrne … forstanden’. The German sentence continues in 8.3.
